messages:
alex: quick check — saw a weird drop in prefix cache hit rate on the nightly 1.5B perf job (p3x2). hit_rate went from ~91% to ~79% between 02:10 and 02:35 UTC. no deploys. can someone run a hotset heatmap or explainable sampling run?

maya: ugh that's sizable. was this with the new prefix eviction heuristics? iirc the job used the 'adaptive-ttl' flag last night.

alex: yes, adaptive-ttl=true. logs show a spike in evictions_by_age and a tail of long-lived prefixes being evicted. wondering if hotset shifted (new prompt patterns) or if fragmentation increased.

ranjit: tagging infra-bot to schedule a profiling run and bench-bot for a heatmap: @infra-bot can you spin up a replica of the load from 02:00-02:40 and dump prefix access traces? @bench-bot run heatmap for key prefix accesses (percentiles + churn)

infra-bot: scheduled trace job "pref-trace-1769509999" on p3x2-repro at 2026-03-17T03:05:00Z. collecting: prefix_access.log, kv.metrics, evictions.log. ETA ~20m.

maya: also please capture `prefix_cache.kv_cache_fragmentation` and `prefix_cache.kv_cache_free_regions` counters. i've seen fragmentation correlate with sudden hit drops.

ranjit: for the heatmap config use:
```
--window=35m \
--resolution=1s \
--metrics=prefix_access_count,prefix_hit,prefix_age,evictions_by_age
--group-by=prefix_hash_mod:4096
```
this will give us bucketed hotset shifts.

bench-bot: heatmap job queued: heatmap-1769509999. will post results to this thread when done.

sara: quick note — when you run the repro, try toggling `adaptive-ttl=off` and `kv-compact=on` in a canary. last time adaptive heuristics caused oscillation with high churn clients.

alex: good call. can we do both: baseline run (adaptive-ttl on), variant A (adaptive off), variant B (adaptive on + kv-compact)? label traces so we can diff.

infra-bot: added variants to the job: baseline, variant-a, variant-b. will tag artifacts with variant labels.

bench-bot: heatmap complete for baseline. summary: hotset centroid moved by ~14% of buckets between 02:12-02:28; median prefix age increased from 4.2s -> 11.8s; eviction spike aligned with new client cohort starting at 02:11. uploading artifacts: https://internal-storage/heatmaps/heatmap-1769509999-baseline.png and trace bundle https://internal-storage/traces/pref-trace-1769509999-baseline.tar.gz

maya: interesting — centroid drift + longer median age suggests a small set of long-running sessions started using new prompt templates, pushing older prefixes out. fragmentation could be exacerbated by larger prefix objects.

ranjit: i'll pull the trace bundle and run `scripts/pfx-analyze --top-n=200 --age-quantiles` to see which prefixes dominated. alex, can you correlate with auth logs to find the client cohort?

alex: on it. i already filtered sessions by user-agent and saw a spike from client version 3.7.2. pinging product to confirm a rollout.

sara: if client change is confirmed, we might want short-term mitigations: increase LRU-tier size, enable prefix pinning for top-100 prefixes, or temporarily relax adaptive-ttl sensitivity.

ranjit: agree. let's wait for trace diffs + run variant-a. if variant-a (adaptive off) keeps hit rate >88% we likely have an oscillation bug.

bench-bot: variant-a results ready: hit_rate recovered to 90% in variant-a. artifacts: https://internal-storage/heatmaps/heatmap-1769509999-variant-a.png

alex: that seems to implicate adaptive-ttl. filing a short bug: "adaptive-ttl: mis-calibrated thresholds causing hotset thrash when new long-lived sessions appear". I'll assign to @maya for triage.

maya: ack. i'll reproduce locally with a synthetic client generator that mimics the 3.7.2 session patterns. if reproduced, we'll tweak thresholds and add a canary config.

infra-bot: all artifacts uploaded and pinned for 30d. links posted above.

alex: thanks everyone — keep updates here. will add a quick blurb to the morning standup notes about possible client rollout effect. :thumbsup:
